- [research/recovered/practical_comments103/comments/comment_6573466153.md:8](../../research/recovered/practical_comments103/comments/comment_6573466153.md?plain=1#L8-L8) — 2. On the zero branch `0x40E2D1 PUSH EBX; 0x40E2D2 CALL 0x48EEE0`. The callee prologue `0x48EF07 MOV EBP,[ESP+0x4C]` reads the first stack argument (after its 0x48 bytes of prologue stack allocation), so **on this caller** `EBP=EBX`. The callee reads `0x48EF84 CMP BYTE [EBP+0x1EEC71],0`, and selected paths write **the same address**, including `0x48EF5F MOV BYTE [EBP+0x1EEC71],0` and `0x48F00B MOV BYTE [EBP+0x1EEC71],1`. These writes are conditional, NOT unconditional success/commit events.
